title: How a Finger Clip Reads Your Blood Oxygen ❤️ #shorts
description:
A pulse oximeter clips on your finger and reads your blood oxygen in seconds, without a needle. One side shines red light (about 660 nm) and invisible infrared (about 940 nm) through your finger, and a sensor on the other side measures what gets through. Oxygen-rich hemoglobin absorbs more infrared; oxygen-poor hemoglobin absorbs more red, so the ratio tells the device how saturated your blood is. To ignore skin, bone and veins, it only looks at the part of the signal that pulses with each heartbeat: the arterial blood. That's also why movement, cold fingers or poor circulation can make readings less reliable.

This is a general explainer, not medical advice.
